text:
Kris Letang is 39, three Cups and a Masterton into a career spent entirely in Pittsburgh, and he's still playing 20 minutes a night. He has no goals and 7 assists in 17 games, two of them in Saturday's win in Los Angeles.

The goals may not come. He has 1.56 expected goals on 32 shots, so a blank isn't far off his chances, though he usually finds a few. The playmaking is the part worth watching. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season put him in the 93rd percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists, and the Penguins take 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, almost five points better than without him.

The less flattering view: Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, and Pittsburgh has scored about 3.6 more goals than its chances deserve with him out there. Our numbers project about 34 points, right in line with last year. What keeps us interested is that the 1,246-game veteran still passes like a much younger player. Whether the legs hold up through February is the question.
headline: Letang, at 39, still moving it
